key_insight: GENIUS introduces a focused benchmark to measure Generative Fluid Intelligence (GFI) — a model's ability to induce patterns, reason under constraints, and adapt to novel, on-the-fly scenarios — revealing gaps that standard 'crystallized' benchmarks miss.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal benchmarks mainly test memorized knowledge and fixed schemas; GENIUS fills the gap by providing tasks and metrics that evaluate models' real-time pattern induction, constraint reasoning, and adaptive generative behavior.
method: Design a suite of procedurally generated, multimodal tasks that require pattern induction, rule inference, and constrained generation (novel combinations not seen during training).
Define evaluation metrics targeting generative fidelity, rule-consistency, generalization to novel constraints, and adaptation speed.
Release baselines, evaluation tools, and reproducible workflows to measure and compare UMMs on GFI-specific capabilities.
impact: GENIUS gives researchers and engineers a targeted way to diagnose and improve models' adaptive generative reasoning, guiding development of UMMs that generalize beyond memorized examples and handle novel constraints in real applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram contrasting Crystallized Intelligence vs Generative Fluid Intelligence with example tasks for each.
Example task panel: input (multimodal prompt + constraints) → desired generative output → scoring rubric.
Flowchart of the benchmark pipeline: procedural task generator → model under test → evaluator → metric suite/leaderboard.
Heatmap/leaderboard visualizing model performance across GFI subskills (pattern induction, constraint reasoning, adaptation).
paper_title: GENIUS: Generative Fluid Intelligence Evaluation Suite
paper_authors: Ruichuan An, Sihan Yang, Ziyu Guo, Wei Dai, Zijun Shen
